sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Paper birch is a deciduous North American tree, typically about 21–24 m tall with a trunk around 25–30 cm in diameter. Mature bark is white and peels in thin, papery layers; leaves are about 5–12 cm long. It is common across Canada and the northern United States, reaching farther south in the Appalachians.

sections.title: Uses and image
sections.text: The bark has documented material and cultural uses, and sap has been used as food or drink in some contexts; these traditional accounts are not a general harvesting recommendation. The plate's white peeling bark, catkins and small winged fruits fit the species.

sections.title: Related birches
sections.text: Betula pubescens is another birch with pale bark, but its young shoots and leaves are hairy and it often occupies wetter ground. The catalogue's Betula entry represents the genus without assigning a particular species.
